chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every act of kindness is a charity, and the one who points to the goodness is similar to its doer, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Loves the rescuers of the grief-stricken.'

key_terms.الدَّالُّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ: The one who points to/guides to goodness

ai.seo_question: What constitutes charity in Shia Islam beyond financial giving?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith expands the definition of sadaqah beyond material giving to encompass all acts of kindness, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the ubiquity of charity in daily life. It further establishes the principle of 'shirkah' (partnership) in reward, where guiding another to good is counted as if one performed it, underscoring the social responsibility of the believer. The mention of Allah loving those who relieve the distressed highlights the spiritual merit of empathy and active assistance in alleviating human suffering.
